description: Imports surveys and their survey responses from the Iterate (iteratehq.com) customer-feedback survey platform.

spec.apiVersionPinning: two layers: a fixed `/api/v1` path segment in the base URL, plus a `v` query parameter (date-stamp value 20250130) sent on every request; a code comment states the `v` param does not appear to be required for requests to succeed

configFields.name: credentials.credentials_title
configFields.description: Discriminator constant, always "Private App Credentials"; the union has exactly one member.

configFields.name: credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Iterate private-app access token, sent verbatim in the x-api-key header.

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO-8601 duration between updates for this resource; connector ships PT5M as the initial value for both bindings.

pathPlaceholders.survey_id: the `id` field of each record returned by the surveys snapshot, which is re-run as a parent sweep before this stream is emitted

authTierRationale: The only credential mode is a single self-serve Iterate private-app access token (EndpointConfig.credentials is the CDK's AccessToken model, a one-member discriminated union). The connector explicitly passes oauth_spec=None to TokenSource and returns oauth2=None from spec(), so no OAuth app registration or refresh token is ever required. The token is sent raw in the x-api-key header (the CDK omits the token-type prefix whenever authorization_header is not the default "Authorization"). One secret, no app registration => T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: survey_responses is a parent-scoped stream: each sync re-runs the full surveys snapshot to enumerate survey ids, then fans out one paginated responses walk per survey. The PullSpec's `pathPlaceholders` names the placeholder but cannot express that the parent is another *declared stream of this same connector*, nor that the fan-out multiplies request volume by the survey count and re-pays the parent request on every 5-minute tick.

Version pinning here is a *query parameter* (`v=20250130`) that is also carried in every stream's `params`, in addition to the `/v1` path segment. The schema has one string slot for apiVersionPinning, so the fact that the same pin is duplicated into per-stream params (and that the connector's own comment says it may be optional) has to be prose rather than structure.

Both bindings are CDK `fetch_snapshot` resources with a tombstone document, so `snapshot_with_tombstone` fits, but the deletion semantics live in the *document schema* (a JSON-Schema if/then reduce annotation with strategy merge + delete:true), not in the pull spec. There is no field to record that deletes are expressed as a reduction annotation rather than as emitted delete events.

The surveys endpoint is fetched with a single unpaginated request and its envelope model (SurveysResponse) has no links/cursor field at all, while the sibling responses endpoint on the same API does paginate with page[cursor]. `{"type":"none"}` records what the code does but cannot record that this may be an unhandled truncation risk if the upstream API ever paginates /surveys.

proposedShape.riskNote: sibling endpoint on same API paginates; no envelope field is inspected here

transports[0].spec.apiVersionPinning.snippet:
# The docs mention that every request needs a "v" query param that's the date
# of the implementation. It doesn't seem like this is required for API requests
VERSION = 20250130

streams[1].pull.snapshot.path.snippet:
async for survey in snapshot_surveys(http, log):
    survey_id = getattr(survey, "id")
    url = f"{API}/surveys/{survey_id}/responses"

streams[1].pull.snapshot.paginator.snippet:
cursor = query_params.get("page[cursor]", None)
cursor = _extract_next_page_cursor(response.links.next)
params["page[cursor]"] = cursor

streams[1].pull.snapshot.paginator.termi.snippet:
# links is not present on the last page of results.
links: Links | None = None

abstained.streams[*].cursorField: Both bindings are pure snapshot resources (fetch_snapshot + tombstone) with no ResourceState cursor and no time-filter request parameter anywhere in api.py; there is no incremental leg to carry a cursor field.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental: The connector implements no incremental mode at all — FULL_REFRESH_RESOURCES is the entire resource list and neither api.py function accepts or emits a LogCursor.
abstained.streams[*].pull.backfill: There is no historical/ongoing split; each tick re-reads the whole collection, so the pull belongs in `snapshot` per rule for v2.1 and `backfill` is deliberately null rather than a stand-in.
abstained.streams[1].pull.snapshot.paginator.pageS: No page-size or limit parameter is ever sent; page size is whatever the Iterate API defaults to and is not observable from the code.
abstained.streams[0].pull.snapshot.paginator (whet: Recorded as type `none` because that is literally what the code does, but SurveysResponse ignores extra envelope fields (extra="ignore"), so a `links` object could exist on /surveys and be silently discarded. Cannot confirm from source whether /surveys paginates upstream.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No headers are set beyond the auth header injected by the CDK; the connector passes no `headers` argument to http.request.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Interval is a per-binding ResourceConfig field (default PT0S from the CDK, overridden to PT5M by the connector's initial_config), so there is no connector-wide default to record.
abstained.streams[1].pull.snapshot.paginator.token: Not abstained — recorded implicitly as a query param; noted here only because the schema's Paginator cursor variant lists `tokenTo` in prose but omits it from the cursor member's field list, so it is carried by `cursorParam`.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static (a hardcoded two-entry list); the connector's `discover` RPC merely echoes that fixed list, so there is no discovery mechanism to describe.
